summary: The CreateUser HTTP handler has multiple critical issues: all errors from io.ReadAll, json.Unmarshal, sql.Open, and db.Exec are silently discarded using blank identifiers (_). It also has a SQL injection vulnerability through string concatenation, performs an unsafe type assertion without checking, and opens a new database connection on every request instead of reusing a connection pool.

items.description: All error returns are silently discarded using blank identifiers. Handle errors from io.ReadAll, json.Unmarshal, sql.Open, and db.Exec properly with if err != nil checks and appropriate HTTP error responses.
SQL injection vulnerability: username is concatenated directly into the INSERT statement. Use parameterized queries: db.Exec('INSERT INTO users (username) VALUES ($1)', username).
Unsafe type assertion user['username'].(string) will panic if the key is missing or not a string. Use the comma-ok pattern: username, ok := user['username'].(string); if !ok { ... }.
Opening a new database connection on every request is inefficient. Use a shared connection pool (sql.DB) injected via dependency injection or a package-level variable.
